[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"GitOps Principles and Paradigm Shifts"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to GitOps"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"GitOps is an operational framework that takes DevOps best practices used for application development--such as version control, collaboration, CI/CD, and compliance--and applies them to infrastructure automation. In a GitOps model, Git serves as the single source of truth for declarative infrastructure and applications."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"The Core Principles of GitOps"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"1. Declarative Description: The entire system must be described declaratively, from infrastructure to applications, stored securely in version control."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"2. Versioned and Immutable Storage: State is stored in Git, which enforces immutability, versioning, and a complete audit trail of all changes."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"3. Automated Software Delivery: Approved changes in Git are automatically applied to the target systems by software agents."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"4. Continuous Reconciliation: Software agents continuously monitor the actual system state against the desired state in Git and alert or correct drift."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"The Paradigm Shift: Push vs. Pull"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Traditional CI/CD pipelines use a push-based model where the CI system (e.g., Jenkins, GitHub Actions) pushes new deployment artifacts and commands directly to production clusters. This requires storing cluster credentials inside external CI systems, expanding the security attack surface."},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"GitOps shifts to a pull-based model. An agent (such as Argo CD or Flux) runs inside the target cluster, watches the Git repository for changes, and pulls the configurations down to apply them locally. No external entity needs direct access to the cluster management API."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Example: Declarative Kubernetes Manifest"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sample-app
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: sample-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: sample-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:1.21.6"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"By adopting GitOps principles, organizations achieve higher system security, faster recovery times through Git rollbacks, and simplified developer workflows where infrastructure configuration management mimics standard code reviews."}]
